test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 19 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Drought Prone Areas programme (DPAP)?

options.text: It emphasized on land development programmes and afforestation.
It was initiated during the Fifth Five-Year Plan.
It provided employment to the people in drought-prone areas.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It emphasized on irrigation projects**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP) was initiated during the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74).
 
• It emphasized on activities like land development programmes, afforestation, and soil and water conservation.
 
• The programme aimed at providing employment to the people in drought-prone areas.
 
• The focus was not primarily on irrigation projects, but rather on measures to conserve soil and water and improve land productivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP)**

 
 
• The Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP) is one of the oldest area development programmes in India, started in 1973.
 
• The main objective of DPAP is to minimize the adverse effects of drought on the production of crops, livestock, and productivity of land, water, and human resources, ultimately leading to the drought-proofing of the affected areas.
 
• It also aims to promote overall economic development and improve the socio-economic conditions of the resource-poor and disadvantaged sections inhabiting the programme areas.
 
• Emphasis is on non-irrigation-based measures like water conservation, afforestation, and soil health improvement.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation Projects**
 
 
• Irrigation projects typically involve the construction of dams, canals, and other infrastructure to provide water for agriculture.
 
• These projects are crucial in areas with inconsistent rainfall to ensure a stable supply of water for crops.
 
• However, the DPAP focused more on land management and conservation practices rather than large-scale irrigation infrastructure.
